newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up, C Bank sells dollars.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up, C Bank sells dollars.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended higher on Monday after the Central Bank adjusted downwards its offer rate for the dollar to 26.379 from 26.39 pesos.
Despite the downward adjustment, the Central Bank had to sell about $75 million to $87 million at 26.38/26.379 for delivery on Tuesday and at 26.375 for delivery today.
The peso settled at 26.379 to the dollar from 26.39, with volume down to $261.5 million from $442.6 million.

"We still think the Central Bank is allowing the peso to slightly depreciate," a dealer said, since its current dollar offer rate is more expensive when adjusted for the timetable of delivery of dollars.
Last Friday, the peso was hit by speculation after the Central bank raised its offer rate for the dollar to 26.39 from 26.375. The rate was good for Monday delivery.
Its current offer rate of 26.379 is for delivery on Tuesday.
The Central Bank said its move was to discourage banks from arbitraging at the expense of the Central Bank.
"The trend is really up (for the dollar). He just made arbitrage as an excuse," another trader said.
Other traders said banks had been buying dollars ahead of the treasury bills auction on Monday as they had anticipated a further fall in interest rates.

Others said they were covering positions after short selling the dollar on Friday to take advantage of the higher dollar rate. "We took the chance the Central Bank will lower the selling rate," one trader said.
